instructions: Slice the onion. Peel and slice the ginger and peel the 5 garlic cloves. Slice the 4 tomatoes. Cut the paneer into 3/4 inch cubes. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium and add the 2 cardamom pods, the onion, ginger and garlic. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion turns see through.
Add the tomatoes, the 15 cashews and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cover and cook for about 7 minutes, until the tomatoes have broken down and gone mushy. If the pan looks dry, add a splash of water.

Stir in the 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder, 1 tsp coriander and 1/2 tsp of the garam masala. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it smells fragrant. Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for about 10 minutes.
Pour 1 cup cold water into a blender and transfer the tomato mixture into it. Blend for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's completely smooth.
Wipe out the skillet. Melt the 2 tbsp butter in it over low heat and add the bay leaf, cinnamon stick and 3 cloves. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell warm.
Set a strainer over the skillet and pour the blended sauce through it, pressing it through with a spoon. Throw away what's left in the strainer.

Stir in 1/2 cup water and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cover and simmer over medium for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until it's a little thick but still pours. You'll see small pools of butter on top when it's ready.

Fish out the bay leaf, cinnamon stick and cloves. Stir in the 1 tsp sugar, the remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala and the paneer. Rub the 1 1/2 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan so it falls in crushed.
Cover and cook over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the paneer is warmed through and soft. Take the pan off the heat and stir in 3 tbsp of the cream.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Drizzle the last 1 tbsp of the cream over the top and scatter the cilantro over it. Serve with naan or basmati rice.
method_notes: All three read versions cook onion, ginger, garlic, tomatoes and cashews until soft, blend them smooth, simmer the sauce in butter with Kashmiri chili and garam masala, then finish with paneer, kasuri methi, a little sugar and cream. Swasthi's Recipes (the lead) cooks the ground spices into the tomato mix before blending, strains the puree into butter with bay, cinnamon and cloves and simmers it for 10 to 12 minutes. Hebbar's Kitchen boils the tomato mix in water before grinding and adds turmeric and cumin with the butter, and Cook with Manali adds cardamom powder and an optional spoonful of tomato paste. This follows the lead's method and ratios for 4, with all 12 oz of a standard package of paneer.
